content:
Based on traffic analytics from 9to5Mac, Apple is testing iOS 27.0.1. iPhone users are expected to receive this update in the coming days, which is anticipated to mainly include bug fixes and performance improvements.

iOS 27.0.1 is about to launch

iOS 27.0.1 started appearing in 9to5Mac's traffic analytics a few days ago. MacRumors has also reported the same situation.

9to5Mac this morning cited Apple, stating that a software update will be released early next week to fix an issue where some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices restart after Face ID recognition fails.

We reported on this issue a few days ago, explaining that this happens when you try to use Face ID to open apps like 'Passwords'. If Face ID recognition fails, your iPhone may suddenly restart.

My iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max has never experienced this issue, but it's obvious that quite a few users have been affected. The good news is that this bug can be fixed through a software update, rather than being a hardware fault.

iOS 27.0.1 is very likely to resolve the aforementioned issue, but it has not been confirmed yet. This update may also include other bug fixes affecting iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.

Since upgrading to iOS 27, have you encountered any issues? Or are there any iPhone 18 Pro-exclusive problems? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
